newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK BROKERAGES RESUME TRADE, BOURSE IN UPROAR.
newsitem.headline: BANK BROKERAGES RESUME TRADE, BOURSE IN UPROAR.

text.p: Five bank brokerages began trade at the Athens bourse about 15 minutes before its normal closing hour causing an uproar as other non-bank brokers were vehemently opposed shouting "disgrace" right after the first trade went through.
The benchmark Athens general share index was up 0.09 percent at 918.91 on turnover of 1.71 million drachmas. Reuters screens showed trades in four bank shares only.
Brokers at the exchange, opposing the move by the five banks to order their brokerages to resume trade were shouting expletives, strongly opposed to the move.

"This is ridiculous. The government is putting pressure on them to trade. This will make the existing mess worse. It is a clear move for a cover up," a broker who asked to stay anonymous told Reuters.
Another broker at Kanaris Securities said the great majority wanted cleansing at the bourse now to prevent the same problems occuring in the future, referring to thje Delta Securities scandal.

"Our demand is the improvement of control mechanisms. The great majority of the brokerage community is firmly against the resumption of trade before the present situation is cleared up," the broker said.
Some brokers said that brokerages Alpha Credit and Ergo Bank were present but not trading. The three state bank brokerages were continuing to trade despite criticism by colleagues.
Others were concerned that the move could be construed as a move to force open the bourse and cover up a possible scandal at the exchange surrounding the fraud charges against Delta.

"It is unacceptable that there is trading going on at a time when the exchange's credibility is at stake. I fear that this move may be seen by the investment public as an attempt for a cover up," broker Costas Katsoulis at Katsoulis Securities told Reuters.

With several brokerages said to have been counter-parties to trades with Delta, many where questioning the reason behind the decision to resume trade before the settlement mess was fully investigated.

Several brokers said that if trade resumed, open positions, which could help determine the extent of the Delta fraud, could be closed, making discovery difficult. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
